correctness.rationale: For \(n=6r+3\), one has \(m=3r+1\). The field \(\mathbb F_{2^n}\) contains \(\mathbb F_8\), and every nonzero element of that subfield has order dividing seven. Thus \(2^m+3\equiv5\pmod7\), so the sum of \(W_n\) over the three-dimensional subspace \(\mathbb F_8\) is the nontrivial power sum \(\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_8^\times}x^5=0\). This directly violates the definition. The source obstruction polynomial gives the same conclusion because Frobenius \(2^m\) restricts to squaring on \(\mathbb F_8\). Exact GF(8) replay checks both formulations. The bounded replay is not used to justify the infinite quantifier.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly leaves third-order sum-freedom of the Welch family open for arbitrary \(m\ge3\) and supports its conjecture by determinant computations. The accepted theorem converts an infinite arithmetic progression of that conjecture into a structural subfield mechanism, replacing repeated high-degree determinant computations by a canonical witness. Resolving an infinite natural subfamily of a freshly stated conjecture is mathematically motivated and not a routine parameter substitution.
